identity.title: Optimized methodology for CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene knockout in tetraploid potato: targeting StBEL5 as a case study.

content.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 has emerged as a powerful tool for targeted genome editing in plants; however, its application in cultivated potato Solanum tuberosum ssp. tuberosum remains challenging due to its vegetative propagation and complex highly heterozygous tetraploid genome. Availability of whole-genome sequence data for the specific genotype is crucial to ensure complete knockout of all alleles of target genes while minimizing off-target mutations. In this study, using Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of cultivar Desiree, we established a methodology to achieve complete CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene knockout. We show that repeated de novo regeneration could improve editing efficiency by promoting emergence of new mutations. We also present effective strategies for detecting mutations in target genes that may lack clear phenotypic manifestations, applicable to polyploid and potentially mosaic material, and possibly transferable to other crops. Demonstrated through our case study on StBEL5 gene, we propose an optimized, step-by-step methodological guide covering the entire workflow. In addition, we provide a basic phenotypic characterization of S. tuberosum ssp. tuberosum cv. Desiree plants with complete knockout of the StBEL5 gene. StBEL5 is a transcription factor known as one of the key regulators driving tuber formation in S. tuberosum ssp. andigena. Under tested conditions, our mutants unexpectedly showed only slightly delayed onset of tuberization, but their overall tuber yields were comparable to those of wild-type plants. This indicates that in ssp. tuberosum (cv. Desiree), the StBEL5 role in regulating tuber development is less significant than in ssp. andigena.
